doc.title: Jackie Cain and Roy Kral interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

title: Their daughter's death and the silence afterward
summary: Four days after moving in, their daughter dies in an accident; they cannot listen to music for months.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: We are still there. However, the only one unfortunate part of the story is that on May 5th our daughter was killed in an automobile accident.

So we moved in on the first, we were just still living out of suitcases, because we had a job that weekend in New York at a new club that opened, and we came home from the job Saturday night and on Sunday morning we got a call about 6:30 I guess it was, that our daughter was in an accident, get down to the hospital in Tom’s River and so we did.
It’s an hour and a half’s drive.
Prayers, prayers, prayers all the way down there.

You think, never knowing what the outcome was or anything. We get there and walked in and the doctor says sit down, and you know we sat down, and he said we knew something bad was coming but we didn’t think it was going to be that bad. But she was already dead. And we just fell apart. We just crumbled. And then we had to go back to Montclair to tell our daughter, she was waiting.
Because our younger daughter was home.

And so we went back, crying all the way. I’m surprised we even made it back because were just like blubbering. And we get back and we told her and that was a big shock and she went through terrible traumatic changes over it. And we all did. And gee for a couple of months we couldn’t do anything. Our friends were feeding us.
We couldn’t listen to music. We couldn’t play music. It was just too many memories in the music.
So we scraped basement walls and dig in the mud in the garden and do this and do that, and all sorts of pedestrian chores.
Trying to get the house together and whatever. It was hard though. We had to force ourselves. But we had to do it because we had the other girl.
